title: Tenkenas (Ward's Island)
summary: Tenkenas was the Native name recorded for Ward's Island in the East River, formerly also called Great Barcut or Great Barn Island.
history_content: The name appears in a 1637 conveyance involving two East River islands in Hell Gate. The map placement is a general Ward's Island placement and not a boundary for the deeded islands.
translation_content:
Tenkenas is interpreted as forest, woods, bushy, or wild lands, compared with a Delaware word for wooded land.

Why Place Names Matter

“Ethnographic island place names aid in native language revitalization, illustrate cultural values, and provide tangible connections to cultural landscapes and seascapes.”

— National Park Service, Anacapa Island — 'anyapax (2023), Ethnographic Island Place Names section
preservation_content: Tenkenas preserves one of the East River island names connected with seventeenth-century Dutch records and the wider Long Island waterway landscape.
